LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing 3.3 Guided Writing: Spelling (2 sessions) • Correct spelling of words • 
Topic 3.6: Guided Writing: Sentences
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing: Sentences, part of Writing 3.3 Guided Writing: Spelling (2 sessions) • Correct spelling of words •  in Grade 6 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: howing months of the year and fix it on the class wall. Why is it good to write legibly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. list the months of the year in correct sequence,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Sentences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Sentences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate writing for effective communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Sentences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. list the months of the year in correct sequence,

   Guided Writing: Sentences helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary,

   Guided Writing: Sentences helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate writing for effective communication.

   Guided Writing: Sentences helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work in groups to list the months of the year on charts for display in class,

2. compose a short poem on months of the year and activities carried out for each month,

3. create sentences from a given substitution table about months of the year,

4. team up to compete in rearranging jumbled up words to make meaningful sentences related to the theme,

5. work jointly to fill in blanks in sentences using correct words,

6. collaborate to develop a creative chart showing months of the year and fix it on the class wall.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work in groups to list the months of the year on charts for display in class,
2. compose a short poem on months of the year and activities carried out for each month,
3. create sentences from a given substitution table about months of the year,
4. team up to compete in rearranging jumbled up words to make meaningful sentences related to the theme,
5. work jointly to fill in blanks in sentences using correct words,
6. collaborate to develop a creative chart showing months of the year and fix it on the class wall.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing: Sentences together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: This is promoted as the learner explores views when creating sentences from a given

substitution table about months of the year.

• Creativity and imagination: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with creative ideas when developing a creative chart

showing months of the year and fixing it on the class wall.

Values:
Responsibility: This is promoted as the learner cooperates with peers to list the months of the year on charts for display in class.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Nationalism: This is enhanced as the learners accommodate and show kindness to each other as they work in groups when

completing tasks.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of time in months of the year to their learning of concepts on time in Mathematics.
